title: Testing Dependencies and External Services
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of testing dependencies and external services in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to dependency overrides.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers testing dependencies and external services within testing and code quality. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use testing dependencies and external services to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is repeatable checks, explicit expected outcomes, negative cases and actionable diagnostics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Testing Dependencies and External Services matters because it is part of testing and code quality. In practice, focus on repeatable checks, explicit expected outcomes, negative cases and actionable diagnostics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Dependency overrides
items.text: Use dependency overrides as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Replacing database sessions
items.text: Apply replacing database sessions against a disposable database and synthetic data first. Make transaction ownership and cleanup explicit, parameterize values, and verify constraints and behavior after failures before considering a deployment.

items.title: Mocking external APIs
items.text: Use mocking external apis as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Testing authentication dependencies
items.text: Use testing authentication dependencies to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

items.title: Isolating tests from external infrastructure
items.text: Use isolating tests from external infrastructure to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Testing Dependencies and External Services
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open /docs; change the query parameter and observe the injected value.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Dependency overrides”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Testing Dependencies and External Services”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Dependency overrides” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Testing Dependencies and External Services, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Testing Dependencies and External Services belongs to the broader goal of repeatable checks, explicit expected outcomes, negative cases and actionable diagnostics.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
